metaDescription: Six printers for homeschool families, covering ink tank and cartridge models, duplex, document feeders and cost per page for worksheets and lesson plans.
expertTake: The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 is the best overall pick because a homeschool family prints hundreds of pages a month and the tank system keeps that cost low. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the value pick when you need a feeder and fax at a modest outlay. If you print under fifty pages a month, a cheap cartridge model or a library print service will cost you less.
introParagraphs: A homeschool printer works harder than a typical household one. Worksheets, lesson plans, reading logs, maps and art projects arrive in waves, and the machine has to deliver hundreds of pages a month without becoming an ink budget problem.

The right choice depends on volume, on how much color you print, and on whether you scan and copy workbooks. Cost per page, duplex printing and a document feeder usually matter more than raw speed, because a family printer sits idle for long stretches and then runs a long batch on Sunday night.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Wireless Color All-in-One Supertank
products.description:
The ET-2400 is an ink tank printer: you fill reservoirs from bottles rather than buying cartridges, and the box ships with up to two years of ink at typical home use. For a family that prints a full week of worksheets in one go, that structure is the single biggest cost saver in this lineup.

It prints, scans and copies, but it has no document feeder and no automatic duplex, which is the compromise. Next to the Epson WF-2930, you gain far lower running costs and lose the feeder and two-sided printing, so it favors printing volume over scanning workbook chapters.

Ownership means regular use, because dye ink in tanks still dries if the machine sits unused for months, and you should fill the tanks slowly from the keyed bottles. A weekly printing habit, which a homeschool schedule provides anyway, keeps the printhead healthy. Keep a spare bottle set in a cupboard so a long unit study never stalls. The printer is small enough for a kitchen counter, and the scanner glass handles single pages, which is fine for a lone worksheet but slow for a whole workbook chapter.
products.bestFor: Families printing hundreds of pages a month who want the lowest ink cost.
pros: Refillable tanks keep cost per page low
Up to two years of ink in the box
Print, scan and copy in a small body
Wireless setup for phones and laptops
cons: Needs regular use to avoid clogs

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 4-in-1 Wireless Printer with ADF and Fax
products.description:
The TR4720 is a compact four-in-one that prints, copies, scans and faxes, with an automatic document feeder that lets you scan a stack of pages without lifting the lid for each one. For a parent who scans worksheets to share or archive student work, the feeder is the standout feature.

The tradeoff is running cost. It uses cartridges, so a family printing a lot of color will spend noticeably more per page than on the Epson ET-2400. It works as a good fit when printing is moderate and scanning is common.

In ownership terms, it is small and light, easy to set up through the Canon app, and straightforward to replace cartridges. Print something every couple of weeks so the printhead stays clear, and consider the larger XL cartridges to reduce cost per page if your volume climbs. Because the paper tray is modest, load a fresh ream before a big print night rather than topping off mid job. If the family outgrows it, the next step up is a tank model rather than a bigger cartridge printer, since the extra cost per page will dwarf any hardware saving.
products.bestFor: Families that scan workbooks and print at moderate volume.
pros: Auto document feeder for scanning stacks
Fax included for the occasional form
cons: Cartridge ink costs more per page

products.name: Epson Workforce WF-2930 Wireless All-in-One with ADF and Duplex
products.description:
The WF-2930 adds automatic two-sided printing and a document feeder to a compact inkjet body, which cuts paper use in half for packets and reading lists. Epson's heat-free printhead is built for reliability, and the color display makes navigation less of a chore.

Compared with the Canon TR4720, it adds duplex, and compared with the ET-2400, it costs more per page because it uses cartridges. It sits in the middle: not the cheapest to run, not the cheapest to buy, but the one that handles two-sided packets automatically.

It works well in a small home office that doubles as a classroom. Keep the paper tray topped up, clear the occasional paper dust, and print every week or two to keep the printhead healthy. Consider buying the high-yield cartridges to lower page cost. The color display is a quiet convenience for a parent who shares the printer with older students, because the menu is easy to read and the buttons are large. For a family that prints and scans in equal measure, this is the balanced middle option, though it will not beat a tank model once volume passes a few hundred pages.
products.bestFor: Parents who print two-sided packets and scan workbooks.
cons: Cartridge cost per page is higher
Not as cheap to run as a tank

products.name: HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless All-in-One with Two Years of Ink
products.description:
The Smart Tank 5101 is HP's ink tank all-in-one, supplied with enough ink for up to two years of typical home printing. The tanks are built into the body and filled from bottles, so replacement ink arrives only when you actually run low.

Compared with the Epson ET-2400, it follows the same tank logic, with differences in app experience and bottle design rather than in basic economics. It also lacks an automatic feeder, so scanning a long workbook is a manual job.

Owners should note HP's account-based software, which some people find intrusive, and should keep printing regularly so the printhead stays clear. Store spare ink upright, and plan to use only manufacturer ink to keep the warranty intact. Setup runs through a phone app, so a parent should have the account details ready before opening the box. Once running, the printer handles a Monday morning batch of worksheets and a Friday batch of reading logs without much fuss, which is the rhythm most homeschool families follow.
products.bestFor: A big family that wants low ink cost with the ink already in the box.
pros: Up to two years of ink included

products.name: Brother Work Smart 1360 Wireless Color Inkjet with Duplex and ADF
products.description:
The Work Smart 1360 packs automatic duplex printing, a 20-sheet document feeder and cloud app connections into a compact wireless body. For a homeschool setup, scanning to Google Drive or Dropbox is handy when you share lessons or store records.

The tradeoff is again the cartridge system, so cost per page is higher than the tank printers. Against the Epson WF-2930, the Brother matches the duplex and feeder and adds cloud-friendly scanning, so choose between them on ink prices and brand preference.

Plan for a weekly print, keep the 20-sheet feeder clear of staples and curled pages, and store ink cartridges flat until you need them. The compact footprint suits a shelf or desk drawer. Its touchscreen control keeps menus simple for older children who print their own assignments, and the cloud scanning helps when a spouse or tutor needs a copy of the same file. It is a sensible middle choice, but a family printing several hundred pages a month will still do better with a tank model.
products.bestFor: Families that scan to cloud storage and print duplex.

products.name: Epson Workforce Pro WF-4920 Wireless All-in-One 35-Page ADF
products.description:
The WF-4920 is an office-grade inkjet with a 35-page document feeder, automatic duplex, fax and pigment ink. It rates fast for an inkjet, with PrecisionCore heat-free technology aimed at higher-volume printing.

It is the most expensive and largest of this group, so it fits a family that runs big batches, such as co-op classes or multiple students. Pigment ink resists smear and water, which helps for packets that are handled and carried around.

Expect to keep it used regularly and to budget for high-yield cartridges, since its ink cost still exceeds a tank model. A homeschool co-op that prints for several families can justify this machine, and a single-child household probably cannot. Give it a stable surface and a spot near a power strip, since the larger body and the feeder need room to open. Its drawers and trays are sized for real office use, so a co-op teacher who prints weekly packets for ten students will find the capacity noticeably more comfortable than the small family models above.
products.bestFor: Co-ops and large families printing big packets.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A homeschool printer prints a great deal, so ink cost beats hardware cost within a year. Ink tank machines like the Epson ET-2400 and the HP Smart Tank 5101 ship with up to two years of ink, while cartridge models such as the Canon TR4720 cost much more per page. Estimate your monthly pages before choosing, because the break-even favors tanks above roughly 200 pages a month.

Two-sided printing halves paper use for reading packets and handouts. The WF-2930, WF-4920 and Brother Work Smart 1360 include automatic duplex, while the ET-2400 and TR4720 do not. If you print long documents often, duplex pays back in paper and stapling time.

A feeder lets you scan or copy a stack without lifting the lid each time. The Brother 1360 has 20 sheets, the WF-4920 has 35, and the TR4720 and WF-2930 include feeders too. Check the sheet limit, since overfilling is a common jam cause.

Maps, science diagrams and art need color, but many worksheets are black text. Pigment inks like the WF-4920's resist smear, and dye inks give richer photo color. If most printing is black, consider a laser instead, such as the Brother DCP-L2640DW.
Homeschool printing is bursty, with heavy weeks and quiet weeks. Inkjets can clog if idle for weeks, while lasers hold up better. Print a page weekly on any inkjet to keep the printhead healthy.

A family printer often shares a kitchen table or shelf. Compact machines like the Canon TR4720 are easier to place than the WF-4920, and quieter modes slow the speed. Measure the shelf and think about where the printer sits during lessons.

specDecoder.meaning: Tank printers fill built-in reservoirs from bottles, yielding thousands of pages per refill. Cartridge printers use small replaceable cartridges that cost more per page.

specDecoder.watchFor: The WF-4920 and Brother 1360 include it, and the ET-2400 does not.

specDecoder.watchFor: The Brother 1360 holds 20 sheets and the WF-4920 holds 35.

specDecoder.watchFor: The WF-4920 uses pigment ink for office documents.

specDecoder.meaning: The bundled ink supply, which reduces early replacement costs.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Smart Tank 5101 and ET-2400 advertise up to two years in the box.

howWeEvaluated.title: Running cost
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tank and cartridge economics, since homeschool volume makes ink the main expense. The Epson ET-2400 and HP Smart Tank 5101 ranked highest, and cartridge models ranked lower. This follows spec sheet details and common printing economics.

howWeEvaluated.title: Document handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed duplex and feeder features. The WF-4920 with a 35-page feeder led, while the ET-2400 has none. Handling features matter for scanning workbooks and printing packets.

howWeEvaluated.title: Print quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at ink type and typical output. Pigment inks ranked well for text and dye inks for color. Owner feedback patterns stress sharp black text for worksheets.

howWeEvaluated.title: Idle reliability
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how each design copes with quiet weeks, since homeschool use is bursty. Tanks and pigment inks scored well when used weekly. We favored machines whose upkeep is simple.

howWeEvaluated.title: Space and setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared footprint and setup effort, since families often share a table. The compact Canon TR4720 scored high and the larger WF-4920 lower. Wireless setup was assumed on all models.

cards.label: Ink tank
cards.text: The Epson ET-2400 and HP Smart Tank 5101 cost more upfront and far less per page. They suit families that print hundreds of pages a month.

cards.label: Cartridge
cards.text: The Canon TR4720, Epson WF-2930, Brother 1360 and Epson WF-4920 cost less at purchase and more in ink. They add duplex and feeders.

howToChoose.note: Heavy printers pick tanks, scanners and duplex fans pick cartridges.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for low cost per page, sharp black text, and ink that survives quiet weeks. Duplex helps for packets, and a feeder helps with scanning.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Epson ET-2400 is the cost leader for worksheets, and the Brother 1360 is the feature leader. Choose by monthly page count.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Pay extra if you print for a co-op or several students, which points to the WF-4920 or a tank model.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you print a few dozen pages a month, where the TR4720 is enough.

maintenance.why: A short print keeps nozzles open. Bursty school schedules cause most inkjet clogs.
Running dry can damage the printhead. Keep spare ink on hand.
Dust reduces grip and causes skew. Use a damp lint-free cloth.
Staples and curled pages cause misfeeds. Smooth stacks feed more reliably.
Humid paper curls and jams, especially in duplex, so keep reams sealed until needed and fan the stack before loading it.

faq.q: Is a tank printer better for homeschooling?
faq.a: Usually yes. The Epson ET-2400 and HP Smart Tank 5101 ship with up to two years of ink and cost far less per page. Choose cartridges only if volume is low.
It saves paper and stapling for packets. The WF-2930, WF-4920 and Brother 1360 include it, and the ET-2400 does not.

faq.q: Should I buy a laser instead?
faq.a: If most printing is black text, a laser like the Brother DCP-L2640DW is cheap per page and never dries out. Color maps and art favor inkjets.

faq.q: How many pages should I expect to print?
faq.a: It varies, but a family with several students can print hundreds of pages monthly. Over 200 pages, running cost matters more than purchase price.
Inkjet nozzles dry during quiet weeks. A weekly print keeps them clear, which a school schedule provides naturally.

Yes, and a feeder helps. The TR4720, WF-2930, Brother 1360 and WF-4920 include feeders, while tank models need page by page scanning. For a thick workbook, consider photographing pages with a phone instead, which is faster than a flatbed and often good enough for record keeping, though a feeder gives straighter, more consistent pages for a portfolio or a state reporting file.
